title: Group Anagrams
prompt:
Write a function `group_anagrams(words)` that returns a list of lists, each containing words that are anagrams of each other. Preserve first-occurrence order: within each group, list words in the order they appear in the input; order the groups themselves by each group's first occurrence in the input.

group_anagrams(['eat', 'tea', 'tan', 'ate', 'nat', 'bat']) -> [['eat', 'tea', 'ate'], ['tan', 'nat'], ['bat']]

title: LRU Cache
prompt:
Write a function `lru_trace(capacity, ops)` where ops is a list of ("put", key, value) or ("get", key) tuples applied in order to an LRU cache of the given capacity. Return a list of the results of each "get" op in order (use None for a cache miss).

lru_trace(1, [['put', 1, 10], ['get', 1], ['put', 2, 20], ['get', 1]]) -> [10, None]

prompt:

title: Count Triplets (HackerRank warmup)
prompt:
Count index triplets (i, j, k) with i < j < k such that arr[j] == arr[i]*r
and arr[k] == arr[j]*r -- i.e. arr[i], arr[j], arr[k] form a geometric
progression with common ratio r. arr can be up to 10**5 elements -- the
naive O(n^3) triple loop will TLE.

[1, 5, 5, 25, 1], r=5 -> 2   (triplets at indices (0,1,3) and (0,2,3))
[1, 3, 9, 9, 27, 81], r=3 -> 6

    # count index triplets i<j<k where arr[j] == arr[i]*r and arr[k] == arr[j]*r
    # (a geometric progression with common ratio r). arr can be up to 10**5 --
    # the O(n^3) brute force will TLE.
    ...
hint: Walk the array ONCE, treating each element x as the MIDDLE of a potential triplet. Keep two running counters: left (values seen so far, BEFORE this index) and right (values not yet reached, starts as a full count of arr and gets decremented as you pass each element). At x: first decrement right[x] (x itself is no longer 'to the right'), then if x is divisible by r, add left[x // r] * right[x * r] to the total (needed-first count times needed-third count), THEN increment left[x] for future middles. Order matters: decrement right before counting, increment left after.

expenditure[i] is spending on day i, each value in 0..200. For every day
from index d onward, look at the PRECEDING d days (a sliding window) and
compute their median. If today's spending is >= 2 * that median, it's a
fraud notification. Return the total notification count.

expenditure can be up to 2*10**5 days -- re-sorting a d-sized window on
every day (O(n*d log d)) will TLE. The values being bounded to 0..200 is
the hint: use a counting array, not a sort.

    # d: int, lookback window size

    # d days; if today's spend >= 2*median, that's a notification

To find the median, walk v from 0 to 200 accumulating counts until the running total reaches the middle rank(s) (d//2+1 for odd d; average the values at ranks d//2 and d//2+1 for even d) -- 201 is a constant, so this whole scan is O(1) per day, not O(d log d). prompt:

arr[i] > arr[j]. arr can be up to 10**5 elements -- the O(n^2) brute-force
double loop will TLE. Use merge sort's divide-and-conquer to count them in
O(n log n) while sorting.

[2, 1, 3, 1, 2] -> 4

    # an inversion is a pair (i, j) with i < j and arr[i] > arr[j]

    # return: int, total number of inversions

hint: This is min_bribes' 'minimum bribes == total inversions' insight, run backwards through a divide-and-conquer sort instead of a single linear scan. Split the array in half, recursively sort+count each half, then during the MERGE step: whenever you take an element from the right half before the left half is exhausted, EVERY remaining element in the left half is greater than it (both halves are already individually sorted at that point) -- that's `len(left) - i` inversions in one shot, not one at a time. Total inversions = left's inversions + right's inversions + inversions found during this merge.
